# Bank Transfer Process Clause

Controls when a Bank Transfer Contract may request its single transfer. `paymentPolicyAction` is `transfer`. Request eligibility, instruction acceptance, and bank-confirmed completion are separate facts. All paths belong to the instruction document containing the clause, including a nested instruction.

## Transfer policy

Clause configuration uses `parameters` and `bindings` objects. The host must be a Bank Transfer Contract.

- `parameters.method` defaults to `bank-transfer`; `conditional-bank` is also accepted. Both use the same transfer behavior.
- `parameters.transfer` defaults to an empty policy. Its `mode` defaults to `workflow`, which adds no automatic transfer policy. The host's payer workflow remains subject to any existing `paymentTerms.transferGate`.
- With `mode: when`, `parameters.transfer.when` and a nonempty text `parameters.transfer.requestId` are required. The request identifier must also satisfy the transfer function's 128-character limit.

The `when` expression uses a bounded, pure predicate language: static `$document` reads, comparisons, Boolean operators, existence, membership, size, addition, subtraction, and literals. `$nodeBlueId` must directly wrap a static `$document` read. Document paths must be non-root JSON pointers; reads under `/sources/` require the alias in `parameters.sources`. Unsupported operators, dynamic paths, and excessive nesting are rejected.

In `when` mode, the plan initializes `/paymentProcess_{clauseKey}/transferAllowed` to false and points `/paymentTerms/transferGate` to it. A different existing transfer gate causes a configuration conflict. Changes to `/payment`, `/bankTransfer`, `/activation`, `/sourceLinks`, and predicate-read paths reevaluate eligibility; a nonempty `parameters.sources` also enables reevaluation on embedded-document notifications.

The gate becomes true only when `/activation/active` is exactly true, the predicate is exactly true, and either `/clauses/documentSources` is absent or `/sourceLinks/ready` is exactly true. The automatic handler attempts its configured request only while the gate is true, `/payment/accepted` is true, `/payment/closed` is false, and `/bankTransfer/status` is `idle`. Otherwise it makes no request. The gate also guards every new payer-workflow transfer request.

The installed clause's transition validation unconditionally disallows amendments with `PAYMENT_PROCESS_POLICY_IMMUTABLE`, including when its own configuration is unchanged.

## Requests and bank outcomes

The host's `requestTransfer` workflow accepts only `requestId`, a nonempty text value of at most 128 characters. Its caller must match `paymentTerms.payerChannel`; the automatic policy uses the document-rule route. Both require instruction acceptance and, when document sources are configured, source readiness. A new request also requires that payment is not closed and any transfer gate is true.

The transfer uses the full `paymentTerms.amountMinor`, in minor units of `paymentTerms.currency`. The caller does not select a partial amount. Recording a new request stores its identifier, sets `bankTransfer.status` to `requested`, and emits `Bank Transfer Event` with `kind: Transfer Requested`, amount, currency, and identifier. This records an intention, not money movement. Once an identifier is recorded, the same identifier returns `duplicate` after the preceding readiness and acceptance checks; a different identifier is rejected, even after a declined outcome.

Only the caller matching `paymentTerms.guarantorChannel` may report `confirmTransfer`, `declineTransfer`, or `reportTransferUnknown`. Each requires the recorded `requestId` and a nonempty bank `reference` of at most 256 characters. Confirmation additionally requires `amountMinor` and `currency` to exactly match the payment terms. Optional amount and currency fields on declined or unknown reports do not update confirmed money and are not checked for equality with those terms. Public transfer workflows also invoke `Require Active Parties`; its additional admission rules are not supplied here.

`requested` awaits the bank's report. `unknown` records an unresolved outcome that must be reconciled against the same request. Either can transition to `completed` or `declined`, which are terminal. Repeating the same status and reference returns `duplicate`; a conflicting reference for the same status or a different outcome after a terminal result is rejected. `acceptedNew` means a request or outcome report was newly recorded, including an unknown or declined report.

A completed report sets `/payment/completed` to the full instruction amount, copies the bank reference to `/payment/transactionId`, and emits `Payment Completed` with `evidence: bankConfirmation`. Every newly recorded bank outcome also emits `Bank Transfer Event` with `kind: Transfer Outcome`. Completion does not set `/payment/closed`. This process creates no card authorization or capture; a refund requires a separate transfer instruction, so its completed amount is not a net-of-refunds balance.

The supplied definitions use `idle` as the automatic-request prerequisite but do not show initialization of bank-transfer state. Missing status or identifiers must not be treated as `idle` or empty. Shared payment initialization establishes false acceptance/rejection flags and zero completed money only after it runs; neither an absent flag nor an accepted instruction proves transfer completion.

## Inherited action connections

Inherited action `bindings` are dictionaries of named connections. `params` maps inputs, connection `when` can skip execution, and `parameters.conditions` can reject an action. Optional `before` and `after` surround execution; `after` and consumption of `once` occur only for a newly accepted action outcome. `once` defaults to false. Workflow connections use an authenticated `party` or `channel`; their declaration does not grant a particular viewer permission.

Under the bank payment method, inherited `requestAuthorize`, `requestCapture`, `requestRefund`, `requestVoid`, and control-request actions fail the reservation-method guard. `approveRecipient` can record approval only from the currently selected payee's workflow. That approval is separate from bank confirmation, and the bank transfer request path does not check it.
